The modern shape has a 古-like top above the two leg-like strokes 儿, the indexing radical. Modern-shape mnemonic: picture that top standing firmly on two legs to overcome a difficulty. This is a memory aid, not a historical derivation or a phonetic analysis.

source-only for this quiz: 克つ かつ — overcome; prevail; rare spelling of the かつ verb; 己に克つ おのれにかつ — control oneself

Both sourced readings remain in the metadata. Reading questions select コク only. The rarity label concerns the standalone spelling 克つ, not the pronunciation かつ. The self-control expression 己に克つ illustrates the native reading without making every use of 勝つ interchangeable with 克つ.

古 lacks the lower legs; 兄 has 口 above its legs, while 元 has two horizontal lines above them.

勝 also concerns prevailing. Learn 勝つ かつ for winning a contest. 克つ appears in self-control uses such as 己に克つ; this is a useful spelling association, not an absolute division of every meaning between 克 and 勝.

克 contributes overcoming or mastering, and 服 contributes submission or bringing under control here. The related ideas reinforce the meaning in コク + フク. 服 is not "clothes" in this compound.

服 is central to words for clothes. In other vocabulary it also relates to taking medicine or obeying; do not translate it as "clothing" in every compound. In 克服 こくふく, "overcoming; surmounting," it contributes bringing under control, not clothes.
